articles.title_zh: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says
facts_zh:
Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says
- Published
One of two surgeons who treated victims on the streets in the aftermath of a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland said his colleague "undoubtedly" saved the life of a gravely injured police officer.
The pair were eating near the city's Main Market Square on Saturday when a gunman began firing at random, killing six people and injuring 15.
The doctors raced to treat both the attacker and two officers shot while subduing the perpetrator.

facts_zh:
Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
- Published
The Aramco Tower, a skyscraper in the Saudi Arabian capital's central financial district, had been hit by an air attack.
A statement issued via the Houthi-controlled Saba news agency confirmed the group had targeted Riyadh's business zone on Saturday, without mentioning the Aramco Tower by name.
The Saudi energy ministry said the tower had suffered only "minor damage" and no one had been killed or injured.

facts_zh:
Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
- Published
At least seven people have died in a train crash near the Egyptian city of Giza, with more than 100 injured.
The country's railway authority said two trains travelling south from Giza and Cairo collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.
Images from the scene showed people looking inside overturned carriages for injured passengers as a massive emergency response was launched.

articles.title_zh: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least four
facts_zh: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 30 miles from Cairo At least four people were killed and almost 90 others were injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, authorities have said.

The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 30 miles south of Cairo, when a train travelling to the south-western Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transportation ministry.
It said one of the trains derailed.

articles.title_original: Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali
articles.title_zh: Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali
facts_zh:
Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali
- Published
Millions across India are celebrating Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, illuminating homes, temples, offices and streets with oil lamps and colourful lights to symbolise the triumph of light over darkness.
The festival falls on the darkest night of the Hindu lunar month of Kartik, when the moon is not visible in the sky.
Although Diwali traditions vary across India's regions and communities, the festival is widely marked by prayers, family gatherings, the exchange of sweets and the lighting of firecrackers.

all_titles.en: Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali

articles.title_original: Banana producers in Latin America want better pay to cope with effects of climate crisis
articles.title_zh: Banana producers in Latin America want better pay to cope with effects of climate crisis
facts_zh: Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event.

High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body.
In the Dominican Republic, farmers are expected to face drought conditions, with forecasts of drier and warmer than usual conditions.
